issues.description: Transport exceptions such as timeouts and connection failures escape directly and are never retried or wrapped in typed client errors.
Resource IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, so IDs containing slashes or reserved characters can misroute requests.
Retry-After parsing only accepts numeric seconds and ignores the standard HTTP-date form.
backoff_cap is applied before jitter, so the actual sleep can exceed the configured cap.
Retry/backoff configuration is not validated, allowing negative or inconsistent values that can break sleep behavior.
Pagination trusts successful response JSON shape and can raise raw AttributeError or yield malformed items instead of a typed API/client error.
Batch creation trusts the response results key/count/order and can silently return incomplete data or raise raw KeyError on malformed success responses.
BatchItemResult and ReviewResult do not validate literal fields, allowing invalid statuses or verdicts into typed models.
Model parsers use direct indexing and loose casts, so bad API data leaks KeyError or ValueError instead of a controlled parsing error.
Scripted mock responses bypass API-key validation, which can hide auth-header regressions in tests.
Mock JSON body handling assumes decoded JSON is a dict and can crash on valid non-object JSON instead of returning a 400 response.
Dev tooling only includes pytest; there is no configured formatter, linter, type checker, or coverage gate for a typed client library.
